Soccer, footy, touch and Oztag all put big demands on the hip flexors, especially late in a game. A strain usually shows up as pain at the front of the hip or top of the thigh.

Sprinting, kicking and sudden changes of pace ask the quads to lengthen and contract hard at once. For the first few days, walk within comfort, skip hard stretching into the pain, and park sprinting and kicking.

caption:
Ever heard "zip up" in Pilates and quietly wondered what it means? Momo did too. Cues are shortcuts, and plain English helps them land.

"Zip up" is a gentle lower tummy hug, about a third of your effort, like doing up snug jeans, with no breath holding. "Soften your ribs" means breathing out as your arms go overhead so the ribs settle. "Grow tall" lifts the crown of your head, not your chin. "Shoulders away from your ears" is a light suggestion, not a hard pull down.

If a cue doesn't click, ask. A different image or a quick demo often helps. Our Pilates team at Hybrid Physio explains the why behind each move. Book online via the link in bio.

caption:
Momo loves Pilates, but her wrists grumble every time class goes into a plank. Planks and hands and knees work load the wrist while it's bent right back, which is a big ask if your wrists aren't used to it.

The good news: Pilates is easy to adapt. Try forearms or a soft fist instead of a flat hand, press through your finger bases and thumb pad, and pop a folded towel under the heel of your hand. Build tolerance with short holds over a few weeks. Most importantly, tell your instructor at the start of class.

Swelling or tingling fingers are worth getting checked. Our clinical Pilates team at Hybrid Physio tailors sessions to you. Book online via the link in bio.
